The House Budget Committee’s failure to pass their own reconciliation bill proves the GOP’s “cuts” are performative theater. H. Con. Res. 14 claimed $1.5 trillion in savings over a decade, but the Senate gutted it to $4 billion—barely a rounding error in our $6.3 trillion budget.

Slashing pennies from nutrition programs while leaving trillion-dollar bureaucracies untouched isn’t fiscal responsibility—it’s a scam. Real reform requires dismantling entire agencies, not trimming their budgets.

Until Congress stops protecting the administrative state, these votes are just PR stunts to distract from their addiction to spending.

The GOP tax plan replaces a rigged system where lobbyists and bureaucrats pick winners—Fair Tax ends that. H.R. 25 abolishes the IRS, kills payroll taxes, and lets workers keep every dollar they earn until they spend it. The prebate ensures essentials aren’t taxed, unlike Biden’s era where hidden levies bled paychecks dry.

Deficit hawks ignore how D.C. burned $3.8 trillion on foreign wars, DEI grants, and green slush funds while families struggled. Real reform means ending the tax code’s complexity that lets billionaires exploit loopholes.

If Congress wants to cut waste, start with the $500B in Medicare fraud and $200B in hospital price-gouging—not scare tactics about seniors.

Governor Hobbs is missing the point. Medicaid is collapsing under the weight of bureaucratic bloat and systemic abuse by those who never paid into the system. The real crisis isn’t funding cuts—it’s millions exploiting emergency care loopholes while hospitals hemorrhage cash on administrative waste.

The One Big Beautiful Bill’s $1.6T in cuts barely scratch the surface of the $6T needed to fix this. Arizona’s healthcare system bleeds $21B annually, with 75% federally funded.

Instead of fearmongering about reductions, target the real thieves: pharma middlemen overcharging taxpayers, redundant Medicaid consultants, and ER abuse by non-citizens. Reforming entitlement spending could save $500B over a decade—if politicians had the guts to cut actual waste instead of protected grift.
